exactText: I think the shelf life of the current [LLM] paradigm is fairly short, probably three to five years. I think within five years, nobody in their right mind would use them anymore, at least not as the central component of an AI system.
sourceQuote: I think within five years, nobody in their right mind would use them anymore, at least not as the central component of an AI system.
normalizedClaim: By approximately 2030, large language models will no longer be used as the central component of AI systems.
resolutionCriteria: Industry surveys, technical literature, and major AI lab architectures showing LLMs relegated to non-central roles in frontier systems by end of 2030.

exactText: I think within five years, nobody in their right mind would use them anymore, at least not as the central component of an AI system. I think we’re going to see the emergence of a new paradigm for AI architectures, which may not have the limitations of current AI systems.
sourceQuote: we’re going to see the emergence of a new paradigm for AI architectures
normalizedClaim: A new paradigm of AI architectures will emerge within three to five years (by ~2028–2030).
resolutionCriteria: Widespread adoption of non-LLM-centric architectures (e.g., world-model / JEPA-style systems) as the primary approach in leading AI research and products by 2030.

exactText: There's no such thing as AGI. There is human-level AI, but human intelligence is extremely specialised. So calling it general intelligence is complete nonsense.
sourceQuote: There's no such thing as AGI.
normalizedClaim: Artificial General Intelligence as commonly conceived does not exist as a meaningful category because human intelligence is specialized.
resolutionCriteria: Continued absence of a widely accepted operational definition and demonstration of AGI that satisfies LeCun’s critique, or broad scientific consensus rejecting the term, by 2035.

exactText: It's not going to be next year, unlike what some companies in the industry are claiming.
sourceQuote: It's not going to be next year, unlike what some companies in the industry are claiming.
normalizedClaim: Human-level AI will not be achieved in 2027.
resolutionCriteria: No credible claim or demonstration of human-level AI across broad domains accepted by the research community by the end of 2027.

exactText: Maybe the coming decade will be the decade of robotics, maybe we’ll have AI systems that are sufficiently smart to understand how the real world works.
sourceQuote: Maybe the coming decade will be the decade of robotics
normalizedClaim: The decade from roughly 2025–2035 will be characterized as the decade of robotics driven by advances in AI world models.
resolutionCriteria: Significant commercial and research breakthroughs in general-purpose robotics and physical AI, reflected in market size, deployment numbers, and academic consensus by 2035.

exactText: That clearly tells you we're never going to get to human-level intelligence by just training on text. It's never going to happen.
sourceQuote: we're never going to get to human-level intelligence by just training on text. It's never going to happen.
normalizedClaim: Human-level intelligence will never be achieved solely by training systems on text.
resolutionCriteria: Absence of any system reaching broadly accepted human-level intelligence using only text-based training data, confirmed by independent evaluations through 2035.

exactText: At the very best, we might be convinced that we're on a good path towards human intelligence — but not yet at human intelligence — within five years.
sourceQuote: we might be convinced that we're on a good path towards human intelligence — but not yet at human intelligence — within five years.
normalizedClaim: By around 2031, the field may be on a clear path toward human-level intelligence but will not yet have achieved it.
resolutionCriteria: Expert consensus and benchmark performance indicating progress toward but not attainment of human-level AI by end of 2031.

exactText: We’re not going to get to human-level intelligence or superintelligence by scaling up or refining the current paradigm.
sourceQuote: We’re not going to get to human-level intelligence or superintelligence by scaling up or refining the current paradigm.
normalizedClaim: Scaling or refining the current LLM paradigm will not produce human-level intelligence or superintelligence.
resolutionCriteria: Failure of pure scaling approaches to produce systems meeting human-level benchmarks across diverse real-world and physical tasks by 2035, while alternative paradigms show superior progress.

exactText: We have millions of hours of training data to train autonomous cars, and we still don't have level five autonomous driving. So this tells you the basic architecture is not there.
sourceQuote: we still don't have level five autonomous driving. So this tells you the basic architecture is not there.
normalizedClaim: The lack of Level 5 autonomous driving despite massive data indicates that current AI architectures are fundamentally insufficient for real-world intelligence.
resolutionCriteria: Whether Level 5 autonomous driving is widely achieved using LLM-style architectures or requires new world-model architectures, assessed by SAE standards and commercial deployment by 2030.

exactText: If the plan that we’re working on succeeds, with the timetable that we hope, within three to five years we’ll have systems that are a completely different paradigm. They may have some level of common sense.
sourceQuote: within three to five years we’ll have systems that are a completely different paradigm. They may have some level of common sense.
normalizedClaim: Within three to five years (by ~2028–2030), systems based on a new paradigm will exist that possess some level of common sense.
resolutionCriteria: Demonstration of AI systems with measurable common-sense reasoning and world-model capabilities superior to LLMs, published by AMI Labs, Meta, or independent labs by 2030.
